documents.content:
1. STATUTORY MANDATE AND APPLICABILITY
This policy establishes mandatory operational protocols, credentials verification, physical turnstile privileges, loss declarations, and replacement workflows governing official Demo University Smart RFID Identity Cards. Issued by the Campus Safety, Vigilance and Security Department (DEPT-SEC) through the ID Card Issuance & Access Verification Section at the Main Entrance Gate Security Complex, these regulations apply to all registered undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral students, as well as teaching and non-teaching personnel.

2. MANDATORY BADGE DISPLAY AND MULTI-FACILITY ACCESS (POL-ID-CARD)
2.1 Mandatory Physical Display: Enrolled students and staff must visibly wear their authenticated Demo University smart RFID identity badge on an official university lanyard at all times while within university boundaries, academic complexes, dining halls, and transport networks.
2.2 Multi-Facility Integration: The embedded MIFARE RFID chip functions as the master access token integrated with CampusPass (SYS-PASS):
- Main gate speed gates and perimeter turnstiles;
- Central Library entrance gates and automated RFID book checkout kiosks (LIB-POL-001);
- Hostel residential perimeter turnstiles and biometric night gates (HSTL-REG-001);
- Commuter transit verification terminals on university buses (TRANS-POL-001).
2.3 Prohibition of Lending and Proxy Access: Lending, borrowing, or fabricating student ID badges to facilitate unauthorized campus entry, proxy classroom attendance on AttendEdge (POL-ATTEND), or fraudulent mess access is a severe breach of student discipline referred to the Proctorial Board (STU-POL-005).

3. CONTROLLED POLYSEMY DISAMBIGUATION (ID)
Within the university documentation taxonomy, the acronym 'ID' represents two separate entities:
3.1 Student Identity Card / Smart RFID Credential (ID under DEPT-SEC / SEC-POL-001): The tangible contactless credential used for physical gate access, identity verification, library circulation, and security checkpoints;
3.2 Instructional Design (ID under DEPT-ACAD / ACAD-LMS-005): The academic pedagogical methodology governing syllabus chunking, digital rubric formulation, and online course modules within LearnSphere LMS.

4. LOST ID CARD REPORTING AND REPLACEMENT WORKFLOW (PROC-ID-REPLACE / REL-009)
Students who lose or damage their RFID credential must execute the following five-step restoration protocol:
4.1 Step 1 (Immediate Security Deactivation): The student logs into ResolveDesk (SYS-RESOLVE) and logs an urgent ticket under 'Security > Lost ID Card'. The CampusPass engine immediately blacklists the lost RFID chip serial number to prevent unauthorized facility ingress.
4.2 Step 2 (Fee Settlement): The student pays the non-refundable duplicate card issuance fee of Rs. 500 online via PayVarsity (SYS-PAY) under the incidental fees schedule (FIN-POL-002) and saves the generated digital receipt.
4.3 Step 3 (Identity Verification): The student presents the PayVarsity fee receipt along with a recognized government photo ID (Aadhaar, Passport, or Voter ID) at the Central Security Office (Main Entrance Gate).
4.4 Step 4 (Card Printing and Encoding): Security personnel verify active enrollment in UniCampus ERP and print a new smart card encoded with a refreshed RFID chip serial number.
4.5 Step 5 (System Synchronization and SLA): The new credential is issued within forty-eight (48) hours of fee payment. CampusPass automatically synchronizes the new RFID chip identifier with the LibNet library database, DormTrack hostel turnstiles, and TransPass commuter portals.

5. DAMAGED AND DEFECTIVE CARDS
Cards experiencing natural chip failure or antenna degradation within six (6) months of initial admission are replaced free of charge upon physical inspection. Cards suffering visible physical abuse, punching, bending, or deliberate chip tampering incur the full Rs. 500 replacement charge.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND JURISDICTION
This policy regulates vehicular movement, speed ceilings, motor vehicle safety standards, mandatory institutional registration, and designated parking zoning across all campus internal roadways, plazas, and auxiliary parking complexes of Demo University. It is enforced 24/7 by the Traffic & Gate Control Unit of the Campus Safety, Vigilance and Security Department (DEPT-SEC).

2. CAMPUS SPEED CEILINGS AND TRAFFIC SAFETY NORMS
2.1 Speed Limits: Motorized vehicles must strictly adhere to the following internal campus speed limits:
- Campus Arterial Link Roads: Maximum twenty-five kilometers per hour (25 km/h);
- Academic Core Zones, Hostels, and Pedestrian Walkways: Maximum fifteen kilometers per hour (15 km/h).
2.2 Pedestrian Primacy: Pedestrians utilizing zebra crossings, sidewalks, and shared academic plazas maintain absolute right-of-way at all times.
2.3 Mandatory Safety Gear: Operators and pillion riders of two-wheelers must wear certified protective helmets; drivers and passengers in four-wheelers must wear seatbelts. Operating vehicles while using mobile phones or under the influence of alcohol or contraband is strictly prohibited and results in immediate vehicle impoundment and disciplinary action under POL-DISCIPLINE.

3. MANDATORY VEHICLE REGISTRATION AND RFID PASS PROVISIONING
3.1 Online Registration: All commuter students, faculty, and regular staff operating motor vehicles on campus must register vehicle details (make, model, license plate, RC copy, insurance, and driving license) via CampusPass at https://id.demo.edu.internal/vehicle.
3.2 RFID Windshield Tag: Upon document verification by the Security Office, an active RFID vehicle tag is affixed to the front windshield (or two-wheeler fork) within three (3) working days. The RFID tag enables automated barrier gate lifting at authorized campus entry portals.
3.3 First-Year Undergraduate Vehicle Restriction: First-year undergraduate hostel resident students are strictly prohibited from maintaining four-wheel motorized vehicles on campus to prevent parking saturation and encourage pedestrian wellness.

4. DESIGNATED PARKING ZONING AND ACCESS RESTRICTIONS
4.1 West Gate Multi-Level Facility: Primary parking hub for day-scholar student four-wheelers and commuter two-wheelers;
4.2 East Enclave Parking Bays: Designated strictly for hostel residents and residential faculty;
4.3 Chanakya and Ramanujan Administrative Porches: Reserved exclusively for designated executive vehicles, emergency services, and official campus buses;
4.4 Prohibited Zones: Parking in front of building fire exits, emergency hydrants, disability access ramps, delivery bays, or landscaped verges is strictly forbidden.

5. VIOLATIONS, WHEEL CLAMPING, AND PENALTY SCHEDULE (FIN-POL-002)
Security patrols enforce parking regulations using automated mobile license plate recognition and mechanical wheel clamps:
5.1 First Violation (Improper Parking / Failure to Display Tag): Written warning and a monetary fine of Rs. 200 posted to PayVarsity;
5.2 Second Violation (Overspeeding / Reckless Driving / Clamped Vehicle): Mandatory wheel-clamping, fine of Rs. 500, and requirement to execute a written undertaking at the Security Complex;
5.3 Chronic Violations (Three or More Offenses): Total cancellation of campus vehicular access privileges for the remainder of the academic year, with vehicle trespass notices served to external gates.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND REGULATORY REACH
This policy defines procedural safeguards, access verification, external visitor clearance, and overnight facility protocols governing public campus gatherings, inter-collegiate festivals, competitive hackathons, academic conferences, and institutional guest visits. Administered by the Campus Safety, Vigilance and Security Department (DEPT-SEC) in collaboration with the Clubs and Student Activities Council (DEPT-SAC) and Campus Operations (DEPT-OPS).

2. GENERAL VISITOR INGRESS AND CAMPUSPASS REGISTRATION
2.1 Main Gate Checkpoint: All non-university individuals—including parents, alumni, guest lecturers, prospective students, and vendor contractors—must access the campus exclusively through the Main Entrance Security Complex.
2.2 Digital Registration: Visitors must present a valid government-issued photo identity document (Aadhaar, Passport, Driving License). Security personnel issue a dynamic digital QR Visitor Pass via CampusPass (SYS-PASS) specifying the designated host department, destination building, and validity duration.
2.3 Escort and Departure: Visitors must remain within the authorized host sector and surrender their physical visitor badge at the gate reader upon departure; exit timestamps are recorded automatically.

3. STUDENT FESTIVAL AND HACKATHON SECURITY PROTOCOLS (REL-008 / PROC-CLUB-EVENT)
Student organizations conducting technical or cultural fests requiring external participant entry must adhere to the following security provisions:
3.1 Advance Security Vetting: Event organizers must submit the formal Event Sanction approval letter issued by SAC along with participant rosters to the Security Operations Centre at least ten (10) working days prior to the event.
3.2 External Participant Screening: External collegiate participants must present authentic institutional ID cards alongside pre-registered digital entry QR passes generated on CampusPass. Unregistered spot entries are strictly prohibited.
3.3 Night Operation and Curfew Limits: Open-air auditoriums, outdoor festival arenas, and cultural stages must cease public acoustic sound amplification strictly by 10:00 PM. Indoor competitive hackathons hosted in Turing Complex or Newton Hall may operate overnight provided participants remain within secured building perimeters.
3.4 Overnight External Accommodation: Non-university participants are not permitted to reside in regular student hostel dormitories. Approved overnight guests must be lodged in designated hostel guest wings under Warden supervision, with daily room registers endorsed by Security.

4. SECURITY VIGILANCE AND SURVEILLANCE COVERAGE
4.1 Plainclothes Patrols: The Vigilance Squad deploys dedicated security marshals across major event venues, food courts, and transit corridors to prevent substance abuse, ragging infractions, or trespassing.
4.2 Continuous CCTV Recording: High-definition security cameras monitor all entry turnstiles, event foyers, and perimeter gates 24/7; camera feeds are monitored in real time at the Security Operations Centre.
4.3 Emergency Termination Authority: The Chief Security Officer (CSO) reserves statutory authority to suspend or terminate any event immediately in the event of severe disorder, physical altercation, fire hazard, or failure to comply with curfew mandates.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND EMERGENCY SCOPE
This standard operating procedure establishes definitive operational directives, command hierarchies, evacuation pathways, communication chains, and assembly protocols for responding to major on-campus emergencies—including structural fires, hazardous chemical leaks, laboratory explosions, natural disasters, or major infrastructure collapses. Enforced by DEPT-SEC in coordination with Campus Operations (DEPT-OPS) and the Campus Health Centre (DEPT-HEALTH).

2. IMMEDIATE EMERGENCY DISCOVERY AND REPORTING
2.1 Raising the Alarm: Any individual discovering a fire, smoke plume, or life-threatening hazard must immediately break the glass of the nearest Manual Call Point (MCP) fire alarm pull station located along corridor corridors and stairwell exits.
2.2 Emergency Notification: Immediately contact the 24/7 Security Operations Centre Hotline (Extension 100 / Direct Campus Emergency Line: +91-XXXX-EMERG). State clearly:
- Exact building name, floor number, and room/laboratory identifier;
- Nature of the hazard (Electrical fire, Chemical spill, Structural failure);
- Known human casualties or trapped personnel.
2.3 Automated Alarm Transmission: Fire panel activation automatically triggers localized audible sirens, unlatches electromagnetic emergency exit doors, and notifies municipal fire dispatch.

3. EVACUATION DIRECTIVES AND CODE OF CONDUCT
Upon activation of the evacuation alarm, all building occupants must execute immediate, orderly evacuation:
3.1 Cessation of Activity: Instructors, students, and staff must cease all laboratory apparatus, close chemical fume hoods, shut off primary gas valves, and leave personal baggage behind;
3.2 Prohibition of Lifts/Elevators: Under no circumstances may elevators or freight lifts be utilized during a fire evacuation; all descent must occur via designated external fire escape stairwells;
3.3 Orderly Movement: Move swiftly without running, pushing, or overtaking; assist individuals with physical disabilities or mobility impairments;
3.4 Floor Safety Wardens: Appointed Department Safety Wardens sweep classrooms, restrooms, and research bays to ensure complete clearance before exiting last.

4. DESIGNATED CAMPUS EMERGENCY ASSEMBLY POINTS
Evacuees must proceed directly along marked exit pathways to designated open-air assembly zones:
4.1 Assembly Area Alpha: Central Cricket Ground (For occupants of Ramanujan Block, Chanakya Bhavan, and Admin Wing);
4.2 Assembly Area Beta: East Enclave Central Lawn (For occupants of all student residential hostels and East Dining Hall);
4.3 Assembly Area Gamma: Student Activity Centre Plaza (For occupants of Turing Complex, Central Computing Centre, and Mechanical Workshops).

5. INCIDENT COMMAND, HEADCOUNTS, AND MEDICAL TRIAGE
5.1 Accountability Verification: Department Floor Wardens conduct rapid headcount reconciliations against active attendance rosters and report missing personnel to the Incident Commander (CSO) within ten (10) minutes of arrival.
5.2 Emergency Medical Response: The Senior Chief Medical Officer (ROLE-CMO) coordinates emergency ambulance dispatch from the Campus Health Centre, establishing an on-site first-aid triage tent at the perimeter of the assembly area.
5.3 All-Clear Authorization: Re-entry into evacuated buildings is strictly forbidden until the Chief Security Officer and Municipal Fire Chief formally declare an 'All-Clear' over the public address system.
5.4 Mandatory Drills: Full-scale fire evacuation and disaster response drills are conducted semi-annually across all academic blocks and student residences.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND INSTITUTIONAL SCOPE
This standard operating procedure defines formal reporting mechanisms, investigation protocols, CCTV evidentiary retrieval norms, severity classifications, and administrative escalation workflows for security incidents occurring within Demo University premises. Enforced by the Vigilance & Incident Response Squad of DEPT-SEC.

2. CONTROLLED POLYSEMY AND ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION (IR)
Within Demo University systems and institutional documentation, the acronym 'IR' represents three entirely separate institutional concepts:
2.1 Incident Report (IR under DEPT-SEC / SEC-SOP-003): The official security documentation logging theft, physical violence, unauthorized trespassing, substance abuse, vandalism, or campus safety breaches;
2.2 Institutional Repository (IR under DEPT-LIB / LIB-POL-004): The digital research library archive maintaining dissertations, doctoral theses, and faculty scholarship;
2.3 Office of International Relations (IR under DEPT-IRO / IRO-POL-001): The administrative division overseeing international student mobility, foreign semester exchanges, and global institutional MOUs.
- Routing Disambiguation Rule: Searches concerning stolen items, property loss, physical harassment, or security guard responses map strictly to the Security Incident Report (SEC-SOP-003).

3. INCIDENT CLASSIFICATION AND SEVERITY TIERS
Reported security incidents are categorized into three operational tiers:
3.1 Tier 1 (Minor Operational Incidents): Misplaced personal items, unattended bicycle theft at external gates, minor parking scrapes, or perimeter noise complaints. Handled directly by Gate Security Duty Officers within twenty-four (24) hours.
3.2 Tier 2 (Moderate Security Infractions): Forced room entry, theft of computing hardware or lab components, deliberate damage to estate fixtures, or unauthorized visitor access after hours. Preliminary enquiry completed within forty-eight (48) hours; investigative dossier forwarded to the Proctorial Board (STU-POL-005).
3.3 Tier 3 (Critical / Major Offenses): Physical assault, possession or distribution of narcotics/alcohol, ragging incidents (STU-POL-004), weapon possession, or major estate sabotage. Demands instant physical restraint, interim campus suspension, and formal transmission of an FIR to local municipal police with Vice-Chancellor ratification.

4. INCIDENT LODGING PROCEDURE VIA RESOLVEDESK
4.1 Digital Submission: Aggrieved individuals or witnessing staff submit a 'Security Incident Report (IR)' on ResolveDesk at https://resolvedesk.demo.edu.internal under Category: Campus Security > Incident Report.
4.2 Written In-Person Report: In emergency circumstances, complainants report in person to the 24/7 Security Operations Centre at the Main Gate Complex. A duty officer records the initial statement and generates an authenticated IR tracking number.

5. CCTV SURVEILLANCE REVIEW AND EVIDENTIARY ARCHIVING
5.1 Continuous Archiving: The Security Operations Centre maintains a secure 30-calendar-day rolling archive of all campus CCTV cameras (covering gates, corridors, parking lots, and building foyers).
5.2 Access and Extraction Protocol: To protect individual privacy, direct viewing or extraction of CCTV recordings by students or unauthorized staff is strictly prohibited. Footage review requires a formal written request endorsed by the Chief Security Officer (CSO), Proctorial Board Chairperson, or Dean of Student Welfare.
5.3 Evidentiary Preservation: When an IR involves ongoing disciplinary inquiries or criminal prosecution, relevant video segments are digitally extracted, watermarked, cryptographically hashed, and preserved in the secure evidence locker.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND MOBILITY MANDATE
This policy defines the operating schedules, commuter routes, boarding norms, fee assessment structures, and passenger codes of conduct governing the institutional bus fleet operated by the Campus Mobility and Transportation Unit (DEPT-TRANS). The service provides reliable, punctual, and secure daily transit for enrolled day-scholar students and university employees residing in outlying metropolitan sectors.

2. FLEET NETWORK AND OPERATIONAL SCHEDULES
2.1 Route Network: The university operates twelve (12) designated commuter bus routes (Routes 1 through 12) spanning key municipal transit hubs, residential suburbs, and metro interchange nodes.
2.2 Morning Ingress Schedule: All commuter buses depart their respective originating terminal stops between 07:00 AM and 07:30 AM to ensure arrival at the West Gate Transportation Depot strictly by 08:30 AM, guaranteeing timely arrival before the 08:45 AM commencement of Period 1 academic lectures.
2.3 Evening Egress Schedule: Standard evening commuter return fleets depart from the West Gate Depot at 05:15 PM following the conclusion of scheduled laboratory sessions.
2.4 Extended Library Shuttle: A specialized night transit shuttle departs at 07:00 PM on working days to accommodate students and research scholars utilizing the Central Library and computing laboratories.

3. COMMUTER FEE STRUCTURE AND PAYMENT MODES (FIN-POL-001)
3.1 Distance-Tiered Fee Schedule: Annual commuter bus fees are categorized by radial distance zones:
- Zone A (0 to 10 km from campus): Rs. 18,000 per academic year;
- Zone B (11 to 20 km from campus): Rs. 24,000 per academic year;
- Zone C (21 km and above): Rs. 30,000 per academic year.
3.2 Payment Gateway: Bus fees must be settled via the PayVarsity financial portal (SYS-PAY) in full prior to semester commencement or in two equal semester installments.

4. DIGITAL PASS ISSUANCE AND RFID INTEGRATION (REL-016)
4.1 Integrated Smart Credential: Demo University operates a paperless transit boarding mechanism. Upon fee clearance, the TransPass engine syncs authorized route privileges directly to the student's Smart RFID ID Card in CampusPass (SEC-POL-001).
4.2 Boarding Validation: Passengers tap their smart card against the handheld RFID validator terminal held by the bus conductor upon boarding. Cards displaying invalid route codes or unpaid fee flags are denied boarding.

5. PASSENGER CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY SANCTIONS
5.1 Boarding Decorum: Students must board and alight strictly at their officially assigned route stop. Standing on footboards or distracting drivers while the vehicle is in motion is prohibited.
5.2 Seat Reservation Prohibited: Reserving seats for friends by placing bags or notebooks is forbidden; seating is strictly on a first-come, first-served basis.
5.3 Zero-Tolerance Misconduct: Any act of ragging (STU-POL-004), verbal abuse, vandalism to bus upholstery, or carrying hazardous substances on university transit leads to immediate confiscation of the bus pass without fee refund and disciplinary referral to the Proctorial Board.
